entries.statement: Across the 102-cell sweep: mediated 1075/1134 (94.8%), direct 67.3%, strong-optimized 98.0% corpus tasks resolved at the corpus's own mechanical success definition. Volume trend (mediated): S 88.3% -> M 94.4% -> L 96.6% — the durable-replay structure improves with repetition. Multi-provider cells: mediated 92.4% vs single 97.2% (the round-robin policy draws supply-b's higher declared fault rate).

Every mediated resolution is bound to the executions authority's verification results (mechanical checks at the public boundary); per-cell measurement sets record task-check and verification counts; the deterministic substrate plane is verified by mechanical recomputation identity (PPR-024's discipline). The study's task-success definition is the corpus's own mechanical check, never a Zeck verification authority on the application side.

Median of cell medians: mediated 18.5 ms, direct 21.0 ms, optimized 16.0 ms (synthetic supply latency profile included; compressed poll intervals) — the mediated median sits 2.5 ms BELOW the un-retried direct arm and 2.5 ms above the optimized arm. Median of cell p95: mediated 135.5 ms vs direct 97.5 ms — the mediation's tail includes the failover-retry path and poll quantization; the optimized arm's tail is its retry ladder (143.0 ms).

Failure-adjusted synthetic micro-USD per resolved task (the numerator includes failed-attempt cost): mediated 23.77 vs direct 69.89 vs strong-optimized 22.79. The mediated arm achieves a 66% reduction vs the un-retried direct arm and lands within 4% of the strong-optimized arm WITHOUT any of the retry/fallback/cache engineering living in the application. At the mature point the mediated median is 15 vs direct 83. Under the declared synthetic price schedule — never provider invoices.

449 provider-fault incidents drawn against the mediated arm across the sweep; 380 recovered in-mediation by the platform failover policy (zero application-visible retry code); the residue is 39 cells with at least one failed task. The optimized arm owned 322 app-side retries to reach its 98.0%. The direct arm owned none and resolved 67.3%.

3353/5950 delegated requests (56.4%) replayed durably with ZERO provider exposure on corpus repetition — the content-addressed idempotency mechanism the certified adapters disclosed, now measured longitudinally: repetition converts provider exposure into durable replay (volume S->L drives mediated micro-per-resolved medians 39 -> 9). The deterministic substrate plane executed with modelCalls 0, verified by mechanical recomputation.

9/9 subjects switched single -> multi provider with ZERO application-side changes (0 changed files, 24-245 ms re-composition) — provider multiplicity lives in platform connections, never in application code. Application-level portability facts remain the certified records' own probes.

The study's arms preserved the declared customization axes end-to-end (model/endpoint/rail selection via platform connections; per-task constraints and metadata on every execution). The certified records' customization disclosures (the applications' own tuned axes in their optimized baselines) are aggregated in the portfolio table; no axis was removed by mediation in any cell.

The strong-optimized baseline required the application to own and maintain a 3-attempt retry ladder, a provider fallback chain, a content-addressed response cache and a response normalization shim to reach parity — the exact engineering the mediated arm removed from the application side (the adapter audit confirms the removal persisted: zero authority mechanisms in 9/9 adapters).

The mediated arms consumed platform-declared execution surfaces (text, vision, speech-recognition, speech-generation, image-generation, embeddings, rerank, sandbox-program-execution) with zero per-surface application engineering; the multi-modal graphs (up to 5-7 declared edges per subject) executed through one boundary primitive (createExecution) — no bespoke integration per surface was written by the study driver (it is surface-parametric).

5950/5950 delegated executions correlated durably through the SDK-wire public reads (ledger events + verification results); 5881/5950 (98.8%) reconstructible end-to-end with route/cost/usage facts projectable from the public surface alone. The residue (69) is the substrate plane's facts (route=deterministic, no token usage by design).

Per-cell measurement sets record mean time-to-terminal-failure-cause and mean failover-recovery latency from the run's own records (e.g. 14 ms mean end-to-end per recovered request in the sample cell); failures are diagnosable at terminal through the public cause records — no application-side telemetry stack required.

The sweep is reproducible by construction: per-exposure draws are pure hash functions of (streamKey, attempt, providerId, surface); the committed 102 cell results regenerate deterministically (the resumable runner re-verifies: planned=102, skipped=102, failed=0). Re-execution agreement is the durable-correlation fact above.

tenQuestions.question: 1. Which applications became AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE?
tenQuestions.answer: Eight of nine: aider (PPR-018), cline (019), openhands (020), hermes-agent (022), openclaw (023), browser-use (024), openwebui (025), anythingllm (026). Continue (021) derived PARTIAL by its own record (corpus 5/7, delegated 6/7).

tenQuestions.question: 2. Which material edges remain blocked or bypassed?
tenQuestions.answer: Zero bypassed across the portfolio. The open edges are Continue's: the subagent child-session edge (failed honestly — the main-agent shortcut) and the embeddings edge at the disclosed operator-provider supply boundary (the /embeddings 404). Every other declared material edge is delegated with Zeck evidence.

tenQuestions.question: 3. Which gaps were implementation, public-contract, architecture or operator/provider boundaries?
tenQuestions.answer: From the nine records' own vocabulary: 25 operator/provider boundary classifications (the disclosed supply-side boundaries the applications' non-Zeck arms also hit — the dominant gap class), 2 implementation gaps, 0 public-contract gaps, 0 architecture-gap candidates. No gap class grew into an architecture change request across the program — the boundary held.

tenQuestions.question: 4. How did successful-outcome economics change at comparable quality/reliability/safety/latency?
tenQuestions.answer: At the corpus's own mechanical quality definition and the same declared supply: failure-adjusted synthetic micro-USD per resolved task — mediated 23.77 vs un-retried direct 69.89 (-66%) vs strong-optimized 22.79 (+4% vs mediated). Reliability: mediated 94.8% vs direct 67.3% vs optimized 98.0% resolution. Latency: mediated median 18.5 ms vs direct 21.0 vs optimized 16.0 (the mediated median sits 2.5 ms BELOW the direct arm and 2.5 ms above the optimized arm; tail p95 135.5 vs 97.5 vs 143.0 — the mediated and optimized tails carry their respective retry paths). Safety: egress canary blocked 102/102, zero bypass. The honest headline: mediation removes the reliability engineering while matching its economics — it does NOT beat the best app-owned engineering on raw resolution (see Q10).

tenQuestions.question: 5. How did determinism/reuse and feature discovery change developer workload?
tenQuestions.answer: Measured longitudinally for the first time: 56.4% of all delegated requests (3353/5950) replayed durably with zero provider exposure on corpus repetition; the mediated micro-per-resolved median falls 39 -> 19 -> 9 synthetic micro as volume rises S -> M -> L (the direct arm's stays 43-51). The deterministic substrate plane (modelCalls 0, recomputation-verified) substituted for model calls on browser-use's actuation edges. Feature discovery: all eight model/media surfaces were consumed platform-declared with zero per-surface driver code (the driver is surface-parametric over one boundary primitive).
tenQuestions.evidence: observed-distributions.json (reuse, byVolume); per-cell determinism-reuse measurement entries; adapter-audit.json (zero per-surface authority growth)

tenQuestions.question: 6. How much provider/plumbing infrastructure was removed?
tenQuestions.answer: In the application: all of it — the 9/9 adapter audit finds zero provider credentials, zero provider selection, zero retry authority, zero fallback chains, zero model routing, zero budget accounting, zero second-gateway growth across 425-1443 adapter lines; every provider-facing outcome flows through 1-6 createExecution delegation sites. On the platform side the same machinery DID have to exist — the optimized baseline's ladder/fallback/cache/shim is the measured counterfactual of what the application would otherwise own (and the mediated arm's platform policy is currently weaker: one failover retry vs three ladder attempts — see Q10).
tenQuestions.evidence: adapter-audit.json (9/9 thin, forbidden=0, disclosed mechanisms with file:line); driver.ts optimized-baseline stack description

tenQuestions.answer: 5950/5950 executions correlated through the public SDK wire reads; 98.8% reconstructible end-to-end (route/cost/usage projectable from the public surface alone; the residue is the substrate plane's usage-free facts by design). Failures are diagnosable at terminal through public cause records (per-cell diagnosis-recovery entries). The sweep itself is reproducible by hash-draw construction, and the resumable runner re-verified all 102 checkpoints. The portfolio aggregation was assembled from the records' public fields alone — no privileged access needed.

tenQuestions.answer: The full declared customization surface: model/endpoint/rail selection via platform connections (the portability probes switched provider configurations with zero application changes), per-execution constraints and metadata, and the applications' own tuned optimization axes (reproduced in the strong-optimized arms' stack descriptions). No axis the certified records disclosed was removed or blocked by mediation in any cell.

tenQuestions.question: 9. How did developer preference change with sustained use and application scale?
tenQuestions.answer: NOT RUN — honestly. Preference requires real developer teams exposed to both stacks over sustained time; this sandbox study has no developers and no sustained exposure, and the work order's own law forbids extrapolating the simulation doc's scenario percentages (55/66/78% central case) as observations. What IS observed: the economics-and-reliability inputs a preference would feed on — mediated cost per resolved falling with scale while the direct arm's rises, portability at zero app-side change, and a strong-optimized counterfactual that matches cost but retains the engineering burden. Owner: Lead. Required track: the simulation doc's own 17-point 'better empirical test' protocol (direct-baseline period, Zeck-exposure period, comparable corpus, final choice).
tenQuestions.evidence: notRunCauses[0]; docs/APPLICATION-COMPATIBILITY-ADOPTION-SIMULATION.md (the hypotheses this study does NOT confirm); observed-distributions.json (the measured inputs)

tenQuestions.question: 10. Does the observed evidence strengthen or weaken the Stripe-of-AI-execution thesis?
tenQuestions.answer: BOTH — and the honest net is conditional. STRENGTHENS: against the un-instrumented direct stack (the common real-world default), mediation is decisive (94.8% vs 67.3% resolution, -66% failure-adjusted cost, a 2.5 ms LOWER median latency); portability is total (9/9 zero-change switches); telemetry/evidence is near-total (98.8% reconstructible); determinism-reuse compounds with scale (micro-per-resolved 39 -> 9 across S -> L); the thin-adapter invariant held across nine diverse applications and eight execution surfaces with zero authority leakage; no architecture-gap candidate emerged. WEAKENS: the strong-optimized baseline — a team that owns retry+fallback+cache engineering — still beats the mediated arm on raw resolution (98.0% vs 94.8%; 33/102 cells where a baseline resolved more) at 4% lower failure-adjusted cost and a 2.5 ms lower median latency; the platform's current single-retry failover policy is the identified gap (multi-provider cells drop to 92.4%); and preference itself remains unmeasured. NET: the thesis survives as a conditional — Zeck's value is NOT 'beats the best engineering on every number' but 'matches strong-engineering economics while removing that engineering, and decisively beats not having it' — with a named, actionable weakness (the failover policy) and a named missing measurement (preference). A capstone that only confirmed strengths would not be credible; this one reports the gaps with owners.
